title: A yearly cap on the risk left in the network

blocks.text: A regulator agrees a rate case with a utility on one condition: in every year of the plan, the expected failure cost left in the network, after the plan's projects, must not exceed that year's `cap[y]` ($k). The utility's model already chooses start years; it does not yet know about the condition.

What the model has, in the lesson's notation: the plan's years $`Y`$; the start variables $`x_{i,t} \in \{0, 1\}`$, given to you as `x[(i, t)]`; at most one start per project, already written; the network's risk with no project at all in year $`y`$, `base[y]` ($k); and, for each start variable, `cut[(i, t)][y]`: the risk project $`i`$ removes in year $`y`$ if it starts in $`t`$ (0 in the years before it takes effect).

Write the formulation first, in that notation: each new row with its quantifier and its label. Then write `add_risk_caps(model, x, base, cut, cap)` in `cap.py` to add it, and return your rows in a dict keyed by year.
The tests fix a plan and ask the solver whether it is allowed, so any correct formulation passes. About five lines.

cases.says: with no project started, caps equal to the base risk are met and a lower cap in one year is broken
each year must meet its own cap, even when the plan meets the caps' total
a project removes risk in every year after it starts, not only in its start year
risk a started project removes is taken off the year's remaining risk
the plan's last year has a cap like every other year
